The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 22.05.2023.
2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 22.05.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., petitioner was proceeding as rider in his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KK-5434 on BEL Underpass, Mes Ring Road, Jalahalli, Bangalore i.e., from Gorguntepalya and proceeding towards Hebbal. He was riding his motorcycle slowly and cautiously and observing all the traffic rules and riding on the extreme left side of the road, when he reached near BEL Circle underpass, at that time a Car bearing Reg.No.
KA-04-MR-8783 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner without giving any hand signal or indicator and suddenly stopped his Car on the middle of the underpass, endangering to human life, where there is no place for parking the vehicle, caused interrupting other traffic vehicles with negligent manner. Due to the sudden negligent act of the car driver the petitioner fell down from his Scooter and sustained grievous injuries to his face and head. Immediately, he was shifted to M. S.
Ramaiah Memorial Hospital for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment expenses. 
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 25 years, the petitioner was working as Assistant Manager at Teamlease Pvt. Ltd., (Swiggy Insta Mart), Hebbal, Bangalore and earning salary of Rs.30,000/- per month with overtime salary. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.

2 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement. Respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court and he remained placed exparte. 
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The respondent No.1 further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident. The petitioner colluding with a owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 22.05.2023 at about 10.30 p.m., when he was riding the Honda Dio Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-02-KK-5434 on BEL Underpass, Mes Ring Road, Jalahalli, Bangalore i.e., from Gorguntepalya and proceeding towards Hebbal, slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules on the extreme left side of the said road and reached near BEL Circle underpass, at the time,
Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04- MR-8783 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner without giving any signal or indicator and suddenly stopped his Car on the middle of the underpass road, where there is no plce for parking the vehicles, due to the said act of the driver of the Car the petitioner/rider of the scooter dashed to the Car from behind and caused the accident and the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries as alleged by him?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom? 
3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.24 and examined MRD Technician at Ramaiah Memorial Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.25 to Ex.P.27 and examined Senior Executive at Scootsy Logistics Pvt. Ltd., as PW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.P.28 to Ex.P.32 and examined Dr.
Shailesh A. V. Rao as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.33 to Ex.P.35 and also examined MRD at M. S. Ramaiah Medical College Hospital, Bangalore as PW.5 and got marked documents at Ex.P.36 to Ex.P38 and closed their side. On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents. 
6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under; 
Issue No.1: In the affirmative.

3 Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. 
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following: 
:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. Negligence is a specific tort and in any given circumstances, the failure to exercise that care which the circumstances demand, where there is a duty to exercise care, reasonable care must be taken to avoid acts or omissions which can be reasonably foreseen to be likely to cause physical injury to persons or property. In order to succeed in an action for damages/compensation for breach, the aggrieved must establish breach of statutory duty which on the construction of the statute. It is well settled that, those who claim negligence have to prove on the probabilities, as to whether breach or negligence, has caused or materially contributed to the damage suffered by the claimant/s.
10. The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person. It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others. In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act. 
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something. In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do. 
11. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and testimony of the PW.1 and contents of Ex.P.1 which is FIR, Ex.P.10 which is charge sheet, I am of the considered opinion that, due to an actionable negligence of the driver of the offending Car, there was an accident, which resulted the petitioner to sustain grievous injuries. Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending Car in an accident has not contested the petition even after service of notice. Hence, interference can be drawn, respondent No.2 is not disputing involvement of his car in an accident, in which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries. 
12. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 22.05.2023 at about 10.30 p.m.,
petitioner was proceeding as rider in his motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02- KK-5434 on BEL Underpass, Mes Ring Road, Jalahalli, Bangalore i.e., from Gorguntepalya and proceeding towards Hebbal. He was riding his motorcycle slowly and cautiously and observing all the traffic rules and riding on the extreme left side of the road, when he reached near BEL Circle underpass, at that time a Car bearing Reg.No. KA-04-MR- 8783 being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner without giving any hand signal or indicator and suddenly stopped his Car on the middle of the underpass, endangering to human life, where there is no place for parking the vehicle, caused interrupting other traffic vehicles with negligent manner. Due to the sudden negligent act of the car driver the petitioner fell down from his Scooter and sustained grievous injuries to his face and head. 
Accordingly, the Jalahalli Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.161/2023. After completion Sandesha.R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13196527/
4 of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 283 and 338 of IPC.
13. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition. He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P24. Ex.P1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P3 is the Sketch, Ex.P4 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 is the Wound Certificate, Ex.P6 are the IMV Report, Ex.P7 is the Notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P8 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P9 is the Indemnity Bond, Ex.P10 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P11 is the Discharge summary, 
Ex.P12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P13 is the Notarized copy of Driving License,
Ex.P14 is the Notarized copy of PAN Card, Ex.P15 is the Pay-slips, Ex.P16 is the Bank Account Statements, Ex.P17 is the Resignation letter, Ex.P18 is the Resignation acceptance letter, Ex.P19 is the copy of B.E marks card, Ex.P20 is the Provisional Degree Certificate, Ex.P21 is the Convocation Certificate, Ex.P22 is the Advance cum Final settlement receipts, Ex.P23 is the Medical bills and Ex.P24 is the Photos with CD. Ex.P1 to 10 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the Car driver. The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 (Sketch and spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.10,
Charge-Sheet against the driver of the Car U/s. 283 and 338 of IPC. The Ex. P.6 i.e. , certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question. 
14. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 
15. The culpable negligence or rashness can be inferred from the attending circumstances like time of the accident, the width of the road and the nature of road etc. The Ex.P.3 and Ex.P.4 are the S k e t c h a n d spot Mahazar prepared by the Investigating Agency in the presence of pancha/ witnesses. 
As per charge-sheet at Ex.P10, FIR and First Information Statement i.e., Ex.P1 and Ex.P2, the driver of the Car drove his car in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle. The learned counsel for insurance company argued that, the accident is caused due to negligent act of petitioner. But on perusal of materials available on record, it goes to show that, driver of the offending Car parked his car without giving any indicator and accident has taken place during night time. As per the Sec.122 and 126 of M. V. Act it is the duty of the driver of the vehicle to give sufficient indication regarding parking of his vehicle. Admittedly, as stated above, as per the documents available on record, clearly shows that, driver of the offending car has not given any such indication. As such, driver of the offending car violated the rule and thereby due to sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle the present accident has taken place. Moreover, as stated above in this case, insurance company has not challenged the charge-sheet submitted against the offending vehicle or insurance company has not produced any documentary evidence to shift the negligent act on Scootarist i.e., petitioner. On the other hand the petitioner has produced the sufficient documentary and oral evidences to prove that accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-MR-8783 and resulted in grievous injuries to Sandesha. R vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 25 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13196527/
5 petitioner. Therefore, for the above stated reasons, I answer the Issue No.1 in affirmative. 
16. ISSUE No.2: The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and he took treatment. 
Petitioner has stated in the petition that he was suffering from frequent headaches, impaired memory and loss of intelligence. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
17. PAIN AND SUFFERING: In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 23.05.2023 to 25.05.2023 and then he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Medical college and Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 25.05.2023 to 03.06.2023. 
The petitioner has produced the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient for about 10 days. He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5 wound certificate the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature. Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience. Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering. 
18. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summaries issued by M. S. Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bengaluru, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 23.05.2023 to 25.05.2023 and then he was shifted to M. S.
Ramaiah Medical college and Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 25.05.2023 to 03.06.2023 i.e. for total 10 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is further contended that, the injured petitioner was working as Assistant Manager at Teamlease pvt. Ltd., (Swiggy Insta Mart), Hebbal, Bangalore and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month. In order to prove the same, petitioner has produced Ex.P15 salary certificates for the month of April and May 2023 and bank statements of petitioner at Ex.P16 and also examined the Senior Executive/Store Manager at Scootsy Logistics Pvt. Ltd., as PW.3 and he has produced the copy of Identity Card at Ex.P28, Resignation letter of Petitioner as Ex.P.29 and payslips at Ex.P.30 to Ex.P.32. As per Ex.P.15 petitioner was earning Rs.24,572/- p.m. after deductions. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.24,572/- p.m. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.49,144/-
under this head. 
19. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner to prove his disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. Sailesh A. V. Rao in order to substantiate the same, PW.4 who has opined that, total disability of whole body disability at 15%.

6 Admittedly, the PW.4 is not a treated doctor. Same was admitted by the PW.4 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.4 reads as follows :
"You are not treated to the petitioner, witness says yes I am not treated to the petitioner." 
He has sworn that, petitioner has got 15% disability to the whole body but he has not issued the disability certificate. It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability. The said PW.4 doctor is qualified neuro- sergeon and has deposed that petitioner has sustained whole body disability at 15%. The respondent No.1 who has cross-examined the petitioner did not establish as to how the disability was lesser than 15% as assessed by PW.4.
20. The learned counsel for petitioner quoted decision of Hon'ble High court of Karnataka,
Bangalore in MFA NO.1419/2023 between H. P. Nagegowda and Subramanya Kalluraya, wherein Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, 'tribunal has to accept the evidence of neuro-surgoen when the mental faculties of a person is involved'. However, looking to the nature of the injuries as well as in view of above decision it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 13% of disability to the petitioner. PW.2 and PW.5 are only record keeper who have only produced the medical documents and their evidence is formal in nature. 
21. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner/injured has to be determined. 
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his D.O.B is mentioned as 27.03.1998 and accident took place in the year 2023. Accordingly, I assess his age as 25 years at the time of this accident. As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '18'. Hence Rs. 24,572 X 12 X 18 X 13% = Rs.6,89,981/-. Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.6,89,981/-. 
22. MEDICAL EXPENSES: The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 41 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.23 to the tune of Rs.1,71,021/-. The petitioner is entitled for the amount spent for purchasing the medicine. Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,71,021/- towards medical expenses. 
23. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in M. S. Ramaiah Memorial Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 23.05.2023 to 25.05.2023 and then he was shifted to M. S. Ramaiah Medical college and Hospital,
wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 25.05.2023 to 03.06.2023 i.e. for total 10 days. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.

7 24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS AS WELL AS MARRIAGE PROSPECTUS: 
The petitioner was aged about 25 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that she found difficulty in doing day to day works. She might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. During the course of argument, learned counsel for petitioner argued that due to injury marriage prospectus of petitioner have been diminished. Therefore,
considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.50,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness as well as marriage prospectus. 
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-
2 Medical expenses Rs. 1,71,021/-
3 Loss of income during the Rs. 49,144/-
laid up period 4 Loss of income on account of Rs. 6,89,981/-
disability 3 Nutritious food, conveyance Rs. 30,000/-
and attendant charges 5 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 50,000/-
 happiness as well as  marriage prospectus  Total Rs. 10,40,146/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.10,40,146/- under various heads.
25. LIABILITY: As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-MR-8783 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the driver of the said offending car. From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 09.07.2022 to 08.07.2023. Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 22.05.2023. Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident. Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner. 
26. INTEREST: As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%. By relying on the aforesaid decision,

8 6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand. Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative. 
27. ISSUE No.3: In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following: 
:ORDER: 
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs. 
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.10,40,146/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization. 
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest. The respondent No.1 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order. 
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon. 
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years. 
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019. 
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank. Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card. 
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal. 
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal. 
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court. 
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.10,40,146/- with interest @ 6%

The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner with interest.
The respondent No.1 being insurer is liable to deposit the amount before Tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.

Remaining 50% of compensation amount of petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Adhar Card.

In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.

The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
